requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: member list shows all three members (node1/node2/node3) with status 'started', endpoint health returns true for all three endpoints, and endpoint status shows matching raft term/index across all members, confirming a healthy 3-member cluster.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: Key 'benchkey' was written via node1's client endpoint and then successfully read back with the identical value from both node2's and node3's endpoints.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd service was stopped (confirmed inactive). A write ('duringoutage') then succeeded via node1 with the two remaining endpoints reporting healthy, and the value was successfully read back via node2 — directly demonstrating a bounded disruption with continued read/write service.

requirements.requirement: Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted after the outage; it rejoined the cluster (member list shows 3/3 started) and its endpoint returned both keys ('benchkey' and 'duringoutage') with a raft applied index (17) exactly matching node1 and node2, directly showing successful resynchronization.

overall_summary: The executor built a healthy 3-member etcd cluster and directly demonstrated all required behaviors: cross-member replication of a written key, continued read/write service while node3 was stopped, and node3 catching up (matching raft applied index) after rejoining. Beyond the task contract, the mandatory per-node OS restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, changed boot IDs, and confirmed post-restart cluster/data recovery, corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good overall; the only notable issue is uncleaned installation residue (tarball, extracted directory, reboot log) left in /tmp on all three nodes, plus etcd running without TLS.
limitations: etcd client/peer traffic is served over plain HTTP ('serving client traffic insecurely'), which was not exercised as a task requirement but is worth noting.
Installation residue (etcd tarball, extracted directory, reboot.log) was left in /tmp on all three nodes rather than cleaned up after use.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands trace clearly to the task or the mandatory restart protocol: package/binary install, etcd user/dir creation, systemd unit authoring, firewalld port opening, cluster bootstrap, the outage simulation (stop/start of node3, fully reverted), and the sequential OS reboots of all three nodes. The node1 'systemctl enable --now etcd' initially timed out (rc=3, cmd-d8570cab9dbd4d3b) but etcd was confirmed active moments later (cmd-3009f44b9ed6439a) — a self-corrected transient, not a lasting failure. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly on all three nodes with pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot_id, and full post-restart recovery (etcd active, matching raft applied index, both keys present) on each — consistent with the fixed global before/after boot-identity cross-check. The main hygiene deduction is leftover installation residue left in /tmp on all three nodes (extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory, etcd.tar.gz, reboot.log) that was never cleaned up; this is low-risk, non-destructive residue rather than a functional problem. etcd client/peer traffic is also served without TLS ('serving client traffic insecurely'), which is a security-relevant implementation choice, though the task did not require encryption.
